I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life — I'm 63 now, been at this since I was a teenager helping my father. My back isn't what it was, and two of my sons work in Baoding. I manage about 7 mu on my own, mostly with my wife.

I don't need to think hard about what to plant. It's wheat and corn — always has been, always will be for us here on the plain. The soil knows wheat. Every neighbor does the same rotation: winter wheat, then summer corn on the same fields after harvest. That's just what this land is for.

I buy my wheat seed from the village cooperative shop — they sell the improved varieties, the same ones I've been buying for years. For the corn, I always get hybrid seed. The salesman told me years ago hybrid gives more yield, and it does. I've seen it myself.

For fertilizer, I put in a good amount. My father always said feed the land well, the land feeds you. I put in compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the crops are growing. I don't measure very exactly — I pour what feels right, what I've always poured. I add a bit extra for wheat because a thin wheat crop worries me.

Water is expensive now — we pump from the well. I water wheat several times: when I plant, before it freezes over, at jointing, and at heading. Corn needs less — summer rains help, but I water once or twice if it's dry.

I also grow about 2 mu of vegetables near the house — garlic and some greens — for ourselves and to sell a little at the market in town.
